messages.subject: Grouping similar sentences together
parts:
Hi, I was wondering if someone can help me with organizing a bunch of survey questions that came in the form of a csv. So this is the format of the csv. 
Say that survey question 1 has multiple answers to choose from, like (a,b,c,d). In the csv it would look like this. 
respondent Q1 Q1 Q1 Q1
1       a  
2             b    
3                   c
4                         d
5             b
So the output of Q1 is spread over different columns for each possible answer. So I would like to convert this to:
 respondent Q1 
1       a  
2       b    
3       c
4       d
5       b
My problem is not with stacking it together, I mean I haven't figure that out yet, but I think I can find the resources for doing that.
My problem is that not all survey questions follow this format. So Q2 may take up 6 columns, Q3 just one column, etc. 
One possible solution and the one that I would have to resort to if I have nothing better is to hardcode and count how many columns belong to each question and go through the csv, subset for those questions and organize them into single column.
This is a feasible solution, but I would prefer not to when I got like 20 something questions to look at. Therefore I was wondering if there's a way to cluster/group the questions together.
I mean the column names for Q1 is not exactly the same, but very similar. For example:
Q1. How do you feel today? -Good.
Q1. How do you feel today? -Bad.
Basically, I want to facilitate the task of having to figure out how many columns belong to Q1, how many to Q2. Is it possible to use that the column header for the questions are the same and be able to say these 5 columns relate to the same question. 
Thanks!
Kavi

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Grouping similar sentences together
parts:
Hi Kavi,

I think this should do what you’re looking for. It identifies the columns that include “q1” in their names, then goes over each row within those columns and pulls out the unique response within each. The regular expression will avoid counting q10 as part of q1, so you could start to think about automating over all questions in a loop. I’m happy to help with that too, but it would be more productive to know the details of what the dataset looks like before diving into that. Hope this helps.

# Make some fake data to work with
d = data.frame(
    respondent = 1:5,
    q1a = c('a', NA, NA, NA, NA),
    q1b = c(NA, NA, NA, 'b', 'b'),
    q1c = c(NA, 'c', 'c', NA, NA),
    q10 = rep(NA)
)

d$q1 = apply(d[, grep('q1[^(0-9)]', names(d))], 1, function(x) unique(x[!is.na(x)]))
​

-- 
Michael Levy
